validated_results.title: Patterns of meat intake and risk of prostate cancer among African-Americans in a large prospective study.
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort study reporting multivariable-adjusted hazard ratios for processed meat intake and incident prostate cancer risk in African-American men.

extraction.population: African-American men aged 50-71 years from the NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study

sample_size.excerpt: After exclusions, our final analytic cohort was 7,949 African-American men.
sample_size.location: MATERIALS AND METHODS, Study population, paragraph 2

cases.excerpt: Incident prostate cancer cases (n=1,089) were identified through 2006.

design.excerpt: In the large, prospective NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study, we analyzed baseline (1995–1996) data from African-American participants, ages 50–71 years.

timing.location: MATERIALS AND METHODS, Study population, paragraph 1

continent.excerpt: residing in one of six U.S. states (California, Florida, Louisiana, New Jersey, North Carolina, and Pennsylvania) or two metropolitan areas (Atlanta, Georgia, and Detroit, Michigan)
continent.location: MATERIALS AND METHODS, Study population, paragraph 1

ethnicity.excerpt: the association between type of meat intake and prostate cancer risk among African-American men

exposure_measurement.excerpt: A validated 124-item food frequency questionnaire was used to assess a participant's usual dietary intake in the prior 12-months as well as to estimate energy and nutrient intakes.
exposure_measurement.location: MATERIALS AND METHODS, Demographics and behavioral risk factors, paragraph 1
